name: Sigmoid
tagline: Scroll motion without the JavaScript tax: native CSS scroll timelines, spring and S-curve easings as CSS linear(), reduced motion by default. About 2.8 kB for a reveal.
seoTitle: Sigmoid – scroll-driven animations and spring easing for CSS and React
description:
Most scroll animations still run in JavaScript: a listener measures elements and changes styles on every frame. Browsers can now do this themselves with CSS scroll-driven animations. Sigmoid is a small layer on top of that platform feature. Reveals, parallax and scroll-linked effects run on native view and scroll timelines, and a tiny fallback with the same range maths covers browsers that do not have them yet.

With `sigmoid.css` you do not even need JavaScript: write `data-sigmoid="fade-up"` and the browser animates it. The easing curves are the other half: physically correct springs, the logistic S-curve and Bézier curves that work as JavaScript functions and as CSS `linear()`, also together with Motion, GSAP or Tailwind. When people ask their system for reduced motion, Sigmoid shows the content without moving it.

free: reveal, parallax, scrub and a reading progress bar on native CSS view and scroll timelines
Staggered lists and grids with one option, also in CSS with --sigmoid-index
track(): scroll progress as a number for counters, video or canvas
story(): scroll stories with a pinned section and steps, in JavaScript, React or CSS
Horizontal scrolling on the inline axis, for carousels and galleries
splitText(): words and characters that arrive one after another, readable by screen readers
Zero-JavaScript mode: data-sigmoid attributes in one stylesheet
A small fallback with the same range maths as the CSS spec, also inside scroll containers, so every browser looks the same
Physically correct springs, the logistic S-curve and Bézier curves as functions and as CSS linear()
Curves usable with Motion, GSAP, CSS transitions and as a Tailwind CSS v4 theme
A curve editor on packages.sweber.dev: tune, copy as CSS or Tailwind, share by link
React components and hooks: Reveal, Parallax, ScrollProgress, useScrub, useStory
Vue 3 directives and composables: v-reveal, v-parallax, useScrollProgress, useStory
About 2.8 kB for a reveal, 4.5 kB for everything, checked in CI

faq.q: Why not just use Motion or GSAP?
faq.a: Both are excellent and do far more: layout animations, gestures, timelines. If you only need scroll-linked motion and good curves, Sigmoid lets the browser do the work and stays around 2 kB. Its easing curves also work inside Motion and GSAP.
Browsers with CSS scroll-driven animations, such as Chrome, Edge and Safari 26. Others get the JavaScript fallback with the same result. The docs list the details.
Yes. @sweberdev/sigmoid-vue has the v-reveal and v-parallax directives and composables such as useScrollProgress and useStory. Install it next to @sweberdev/sigmoid.

faq.q: Does it work with Next.js and Server Components?
faq.a: Yes. The data-sigmoid attributes work in Server Components without client code. The React components are client components that render one element.
Reveals and parallax are skipped and the content is shown. Only the reading progress bar stays, because it moves only when the user scrolls.
